data.prompt: Which contribution uses this research most effectively?

options.text: “Transportation matters. I have seen that myself.”
options.feedback: Not quite. A personal observation does not use the available research.

options.text: “According to the fictional Community Access Survey from May 2025, 38% of surveyed students reported missing at least one after-school activity because of transportation difficulties. We should consider whether transportation support could improve participation.”
options.feedback: Good choice. This identifies the source and date, describes the fictional finding, and connects it to a possible solution.

options.text: “I found a transportation statistic, but we should discuss a different issue.”
options.feedback: Not quite. Research is less useful when it derails the conversation.

options.text: “The survey proves transportation is the only barrier.”
options.feedback: Not quite. The survey does not establish that transportation is the only barrier.
